scope: Second red-team audit of simulated flower contact-force evidence
summary: The v6 exact contact geometry remains valid, but its force claim is revoked because proximity-derived pad forces were balanced by an externally copied opposite wrench and were not coupled to the rod inverse dynamics.
evidence: v6 selected real Sharpa elastomer vertices within the 3 mm gap, but assigned at least 0.02 N from proximity alone.
Its external force and moment were constructed as the exact negative of those pad forces, guaranteeing balance independently of the rod-required wrench.
The corrected v7 solver constrains nonnegative pad friction-cone forces to match the inverse-rod-required force and moment and propagates the coupling residual into the force gate.
lessons: Exact collision geometry does not make a force physical; contact and object dynamics must share one wrench equation and residual.
limitations: v6 cannot support a force or force-closure success claim despite its valid geometric contacts.
next_actions: Require a coupled pad/rod wrench solve and rerun all 660 frames.
